external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A library member who uses the library app to borrow, renew and reserve books.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members borrow, renew and reserve books through the library app on their phones.
external_entities.notes: The member's authentication to the lending API is not established.

external_entities.name: desk staff
external_entities.description: Library desk staff who manually change loan and member account records through the circulation page.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everyone at the desk uses the same shared login for the circulation page. The password is on a card taped under the desk.
external_entities.notes: The shared desk login and password are used by all desk staff; individual users and branches cannot be distinguished.

processes.name: library app
processes.description: An app on members' phones that calls the lending API for borrowing, renewing and reserving books.
processes.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.
processes.notes: The app's authentication behavior is not stated.

processes.name: self-service kiosk
processes.description: A branch kiosk where members scan their library card and books being borrowed or returned.
processes.source_excerpt: Every branch has self-service kiosks where a member scans their library card and the books they are borrowing or returning.
processes.notes: The kiosk's direct connections other than what arrives at the lending API are unknown.

processes.name: lending API
processes.description: The REST API through which loans are accessed and changed, including the circulation page served to desk staff.
processes.source_excerpt: It's a REST API. JSON in, JSON out. Nothing exotic, no message bus, no second protocol hiding anywhere.
processes.notes: Lending service note says: "The lending API is internal-only." Interview transcript says: "The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet." These are incompatible positive claims about exposure, so exposure is unknown. Priya also said she could not confirm what authentication the API accepts or how it handles rejected calls.

data_stores.name: loans database
data_stores.description: The single database containing members, loans, reservations, names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Names, email addresses, home addresses and every member's full borrowing history live in the loans database.
data_stores.notes: Priya corrected the earlier description of two databases: the reservations database was merged into the loans database and is gone.

data_flows.name: borrow renew reserve
data_flows.description: A member uses the library app to request borrowing, renewal or reservation actions from the lending API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API. It says which book and which member, and the API checks the loan rules and writes the change.
data_flows.notes: The member is the initiator through the app. Authentication is uncertain: Priya said, "I think it checks a token the app gets at sign-in, but I'd have to look."
data_flows.data_description: Member and book details; loan changes and reservation requests.

data_flows.name: send loan returns
data_flows.description: A self-service kiosk sends loan and return events to the lending API as items are scanned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The kiosks send each loan and each return to the lending API.
data_flows.notes: The kiosk's authentication and transport are not stated.
data_flows.data_description: Member card, book, loan and return details.

data_flows.name: change loan records
data_flows.description: Desk staff use the circulation page served by the lending API to extend loans, clear account blocks and mark books returned.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Desk staff can extend a loan, clear a block on a member's account or mark a book as returned by hand, through a circulation page the lending API serves.
data_flows.notes: All desk staff use one shared login, so the individual staff member and branch cannot be identified. The password is kept on a card taped under the desk.
data_flows.data_description: Member account, loan, return and block records.

data_flows.name: read write loans
data_flows.description: The lending API reads and writes the loans database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The API is the only thing that reads or writes it.
data_flows.notes: The API is the only stated reader or writer of the loans database.
data_flows.data_description: Members, loans, reservations and borrowing history, including names, email addresses and home addresses.

trust_boundaries.name: member phone
trust_boundaries.description: A member's phone, where the library app runs; it is outside the library's stated control.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The app on their phone calls the lending API.

trust_boundaries.name: branch network
trust_boundaries.description: The network on which branch kiosks and desk staff operate.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The kiosks sit on the branch network.
trust_boundaries.notes: Desk staff are also stated to work on the branch network.

trust_boundaries.name: council data centre
trust_boundaries.description: The council data-centre zone where the lending API and loans database run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The lending API and the loans database run in the council data centre.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The network through which phones reach the lending API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The phones talk straight to the lending API over the internet.

assumptions.assumption: The loans database contains confidential data because it stores members' names, email addresses, home addresses and full borrowing histories.
assumptions.basis: The interview explicitly states that these personal details and borrowing histories live in the loans database.
